name: S_NAr – Aromatic Nucleophilic Substitution
evaluation:
Use this file ONLY if 'applies_if' tokens are present.
Then try base_rules (top→down). If none match, use default_rule.
After picking a rule, scan all modifiers and apply those that match (tokens OR plain‑text heuristics).
Core heuristics:
• Activation governs rate: o/p‑NO2, CN, CF3, SO2R, COR/CO2R, N‑oxide, or heteroaryl (e.g., pyrimidines, triazines) enable S_NAr.
• Leaving group trend (S_NAr): F ≫ Cl ≳ NO2 ≫ Br, I (rarely operative unless strongly activated).
• Solvent: dry, polar aprotic (DMSO, DMF, DMAc, NMP). Keep water low.
• Base: generate the conjugate base in situ (phenoxide/thiolate/amide/alkoxide). Adjust strength to nucleophile acidity and electrophile activation.
• Steric hindrance near the reaction site or bulky nucleophiles typically require stronger base and/or higher temperature.
• If no strong activation is present, consider metal‑catalyzed alternatives (Pd/Cu/Ni) instead of S_NAr.

default_rule.description: General starter for S_NAr on activated (hetero)aryl electrophiles in polar aprotic solvent.

conditions.base: K2CO3 or Cs2CO3 (2.0–3.0 equiv); adjust to nucleophile pKa
conditions.solvent: DMSO or DMF (dry); alt: DMAc or NMP
conditions.atmosphere: N2 or Ar; keep water low

base_rules.name: Phenols → Aryl ethers (Ar–OAr)
base_rules.description: Phenoxide S_NAr. Works well with aryl F and multi‑EWG aryl/heteroaryl chlorides.

conditions.base: K2CO3 (2.0–3.0 equiv) or Cs2CO3; for hindered/less‑activated: NaH (1.2–1.5 equiv) or KOtBu
conditions.notes: Dry conditions; avoid protic cosolvents which quench phenoxide

base_rules.name: Thiols → Aryl thioethers (Ar–SR)
base_rules.description: Thiolate S_NAr. Usually fastest class; often proceeds at rt on highly activated substrates.

conditions.base: K2CO3 (2.0 equiv) or NaH (1.2 equiv) or Et3N (3.0 equiv for activated aryl F)
conditions.atmosphere: N2; limit O2 to avoid disulfide formation

base_rules.name: Amines → Anilines (Ar–NR2)
base_rules.description: Metal‑free amination via S_NAr; needs activation or aryl F. Use excess amine for weakly nucleophilic partners.

conditions.base: NaOtBu or K2CO3/Cs2CO3 (2.0–3.0 equiv); optionally use amine as co‑base (2–4 equiv)
conditions.solvent: DMF or DMSO; alt: NMP/DMAc for high‑T
conditions.notes: For anilines (weak nucleophiles), prefer stronger base or higher T; watch for over‑arylation on polyfluoroarenes

base_rules.name: Alcohols → Aryl ethers (Ar–OR)
base_rules.description: Alkoxide S_NAr. Requires stronger base than phenols, particularly for secondary/tertiary alcohols.

conditions.base: NaH or KOtBu (1.5–2.0 equiv); alt: K2CO3/Cs2CO3 for activated aryl F
conditions.notes: Exclude moisture; consider slow addition of electrophile to minimize elimination

base_rules.name: Heteroaryl chlorides (e.g., 2,4‑dichloropyrimidines)
base_rules.description: Highly activated electrophiles that react with O/N/S nucleophiles under milder conditions.

conditions.notes: Often selective mono‑substitution; control equivalents to avoid multiple substitutions

modifiers.suggest: Lower temperature and/or weaker base often sufficient (try 60–90 °C, Cs2CO3).
Increase temperature (120–160 °C, sealed in DMAc/NMP) and/or use stronger base (NaH/KOtBu). If still sluggish, consider metal‑catalyzed coupling.
Reduce temperature (rt–80 °C) and/or use weaker base to improve selectivity.
Stronger base (NaH/KOtBu) and higher temperature; choose higher‑boiling solvent (DMAc/NMP).
Limit nucleophile (1.05–1.2 equiv) and run cooler to avoid multiple substitutions; consider stepwise protection/deprotection if selectivity is an issue.
Ensure rigorously dry solvent and base, especially for alkoxide/phenoxide variants.
Exclude air; consider small amount of reducing agent or antioxidant; avoid prolonged exposure to O2 to prevent disulfide formation.
Add 5–10 mol% 18‑crown‑6 with K2CO3 in DMF to enhance phase transfer/solubility.
Microwave 120–180 °C for 5–40 min in sealed vessels (DMAc/NMP) can accelerate sluggish cases.
Use high‑boiling solvent (NMP/DMAc) at 150–180 °C; residence 2–15 min, monitor back‑pressure and precipitation.
Use pressure vessel (MeNH2/NH3 in MeOH or liquid NH3), strong base optional; keep T ≤100 °C to limit over‑arylation.
Use milder base (K2CO3) at lower temperature, shorter times; for O‑nucleophiles prefer NaHCO3 where feasible.
